706634643f82af218d1d0092de5aa76fe5c374874ae12a6d1fea9421db14acb0:
MALICIOUS. Financial solicitation using invisible Unicode tags to break filters.

BEHAVIORAL ANALYSIS

The two Stagehand archives match their exact npm releases byte for byte,
retrieved independently with forager. In each archive all eight extension ZIP
files equal their unpacked dist/extension counterparts. The versions differ in
package/protocol identities and frameLocator/deep-XPath readiness logic; the
other SDK source-map contents, declarations, content script, and helper assets
are identical. This corroborates, but does not substitute for, code analysis.

The SDK exports explicit browser-agent APIs. localBrowser.launch selects an
installed Chrome executable, allocates a loopback debugging port, and creates a
random temporary profile unless the caller supplies a profile. spawnChrome uses
an argument vector, with the calling environment inherited by the child. Local
browser cleanup signals its owned process group (taskkill on Windows) and
removes the temporary profile unless preservation was requested. These actions
are ordinary browser lifecycle management, not payload staging or self-erasure.

CDPClient provisions/finds the extension, attaches to its service-worker target,
registers the __stagehandSendToHost binding, and delivers JSON-RPC messages
through __stagehandReceiveFromHost. The worker starts its RPC transport and
an internal chrome.runtime port heartbeat. Its offscreen heartbeat is local
extension lifecycle traffic, not a network C2 beacon. Runtime initialization
requires browserCdpUrl from the SDK before connecting to a browser. RPCRouter
validates method parameters and dispatches browser operations. There is no
independent hardcoded attacker controller or automatic credential export path.

Cookie get/set/clear, clipboard read/write, screenshots, file selection,
response-body reads, page evaluation, init scripts, input synthesis, and request
interception are consequential caller-directed automation features. LLM act,
observe, and extract operations send page information to configured providers
or the Browserbase model gateway, using supplied model/session credentials.
Tracing exports to the initialized telemetry endpoint. Caller-selected profiles
and existing browser sessions are supported; authorization in an actual
installation is unknown. These capabilities remain detected and are not
cleared merely because the package verdict is BENIGN.

The bundles are readable Rolldown output containing Zod, AI SDK provider
implementations, and OpenTelemetry. The only new Function occurrence in the
worker is Zod's empty-body compilation capability probe. Base64 helpers handle
attachments, screenshots and provider data. Decoded strings include ANSI log
escapes, schema/prototype-key matching, NUL-delimited map keys, and ordinary
constants, not a concealed executable stage. Facts report local-flow analysis
budgets and unresolved helpers; relevant SDK/worker paths were inspected in
source and the source map rather than assuming those projections were complete.
The service-worker content script is fetched through chrome.runtime.getURL,
not downloaded from an external code server. No install lifecycle hook exists.

The loan sample is 167 bytes of email-like plaintext. U+E0020 splits fun|ding
and loa|n; U+E0041 splits cre|dit. All three characters are non-rendering Tags
characters strictly inside ordinary ASCII words. Removing them recovers an
ordinary preapproved business-loan solicitation. Their placement specifically
fractures finance-related keyword bytes while preserving the reader-visible
message. This repeated intentional filter evasion, combined with the financial
solicitation and the externally hostile collection context, tips the verdict to
MALICIOUS. Decoding the three tags yields only ' A ', not executable code or an
agent instruction. The artifact contains no link, attachment, credential form,
sender address, executable, send routine, persistence, or cleanup action.
The final destination and actual delivery circumstances are unknown.

The hostile-trait coverage goal is not a quota. One hostile evasion behavior is
supported for this email. The existing suspicious tag-splicing observation is
retained. Additional phishing/credential-capture, execution, exfiltration, or
spam-sending traits would invent behavior absent from these bytes. Inspection
of facts, decoded characters, and the entire body found no follow-up stage or
reference to retrieve; there is no matcher limitation concealing such a stage.

PROVENANCE AND REFERENCES

Evidence, facts, complete scans, source-map sources and forager provenance are
in /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-90084b2c/scratch/stagehand-review.
Both exact release downloads, the Stagehand homepage, and the referenced GitHub
project were retrieved. The project describes browser-agent automation.
Forager requests to the Browserbase API and Stagehand gateway root URLs returned
404; these are authenticated operation endpoints, not embedded payload URLs.
Those failures establish no runtime response behavior. Documentation and model
API references are explained by the bundled SDKs, not treated as fetched code.

The four direct runtime dependencies were recovered: @browserbasehq/sdk 2.22.0
(the registry-selected version of ^2.16.0), @opentelemetry/api 1.9.1,
@opentelemetry/core 2.9.0, and zod 4.4.3. The SDK range's lower bound 2.16.0 was
also fetched. Their manifests and relevant HTTP/session, environment/config,
validation/JIT paths were inspected. None declares an install hook. The four
selected direct dependencies were also scanned: no hostile/suspicious findings.
A missing lockfile means these downloads do not identify an unknown machine's
actual installed transitive tree. No dependency was installed or sample run.

Browser control, broad all-site/debugger authority, cookie/clipboard access,
script evaluation, disabled browser protections, process creation and extensive
network/provider code could explain an external heuristic malware label for
Stagehand. No unauthorized use, hidden stage or provenance substitution was
found. The source's actual reason for labeling these releases was not provided.

RULE CORRECTIONS AND COVERAGE

- .getCredits() in the Vercel gateway was falsely described as AWS Billing.
  The AWS matcher now binds the receiver to client('billing'). Existing Python
  billing fixtures and the JS GetCreditsCommand alternative remain detected.
  A local imported getCredits helper named billing is not AWS evidence merely
  because of its filename or a comment. The legacy virgil case manifest's
  unqualified-helper positive was already incompatible with the old dotted-call
  matcher; neither version proves AWS. Actual positive controls are used here.
- protocolVersion/serverInfo alone do not establish an MCP handshake. The MCP
  rule now requires a literal date-shaped protocolVersion followed by serverInfo.
  Stagehand uses semantic versions and schema objects. Dated MCP responses and
  the fake-handshake detached-staging attack consumer still match. Dynamic
  version expressions alone are deliberately not treated as protocol identity.
- Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger is a CDP command reference, not a Node test
  harness. The exact observation moved to the DevTools leaf at notable severity.
  The harness's generic OR no longer treats this command alone as test evidence.
- A delete_file string in an AI SDK patch schema names an operation; it does not
  prove filesystem I/O or an agent tool definition. Its identical literal
  observation moved to metadata/lang/source/naming/action. The agent composite
  and the applicable fs/file ancestor consumer retain explicit references.
  Other audited ancestor consumers target PE/PowerShell and cannot see this atom.
- The application/zip literal moved from archive manipulation to data/format/mime.
  Both exact consumers were updated; no directory ancestor selected the old atom.
  The WordPress plugin-webshell upload attack remains detected.
- The offscreen permission description now says 'declares', not 'uses'.
- Added notable CDP cookie set/clear command references and Chromium's client-side
  phishing-detection disable option. Existing cookie reads, clipboard, screenshot,
  input, code generation, execution, network, and cleanup findings remain.
- Added hostile unicode-tag-spliced-financial-email: repeated token splicing,
  an email Subject header, and a financial preapproval offer within 2048 bytes.
  It uses no specimen-specific loan wording, filename, hash or campaign address.
  Its measured precision is 5.2; ordinary loans, normal Unicode and a single tag
  splice do not satisfy it. Existing HTML TAG SPACE evasion coverage is unchanged.

BEFORE / AFTER

comparison.json records all analysis units and every added/lost ID. Counts below
are distinct IDs across the input and its members, including emitted registry
metadata. H = hostile; S = suspicious; N = notable.

Sample       H before/after   S before/after   N before/after   ML probability
77a85e       0 / 0            0 / 0            438 / 439        .7493571 / .7493571
84eb3c       0 / 0            0 / 0            438 / 439        .7493571 / .7493571
706634       0 / 1            1 / 1              1 / 3          .6774748 / .9741821

Each Stagehand outer archive: 435 -> 436 notable; nested extension ZIP: 339 -> 339;
each service-worker copy: 301 -> 301; index.mjs: 126 -> 126; index.d.mts: 10 -> 9.
All Stagehand units retain zero hostile and suspicious findings. The sole
unreplaced declaration-file loss is the unsupported MCP identity claim. Other
material losses are unsupported AWS/MCP claims; three observations were relocated
without severity reductions. No supported attack behavior in these samples was
removed. Corrected shared-rule attack consumers are covered by controls.

All calibrated ML levels remain -1 (benign), including the malicious email.
Atomscan's rule output now reports 1H/1S for the email, while the calibrated ML
classifier still misses it. This disagreement is reported, not compensated by
duplicate/inflated traits. Atomscan also warns that its v18 feature specification
predates the engine's expected v21, a further model limitation.

VERIFICATION

Run python3 testdata/taxonomy/stagehand-unicode-review/check.py for the 17
positive and near-miss controls, including preexisting AWS/Unicode fixtures,
MCP staged-process concealment, and WordPress webshell upload preservation.
The runner scans copies outside testdata because test paths intentionally
suppress some evasion rules. These small controls are explicit synthetic
regression examples, not reconstructed original malware.
Both control runs passed: 17 new controls and the 11 existing
npm-sdk-review/check.py controls.
The existing wordpress-emberstack-upload-webshell-linux.zip attack fixture was
also analyzed after the MIME relocation. Full validation is the final action
after all edits, comparisons, and verdict markers.
